The Most Useful UX Resource I've Found This Year

product-design June 6, 2026 2 min read

As designers, we are constantly looking for inspiration, frameworks, and practical advice that helps us create better products. Recently, I came across Razorpay's "Fix My Itch" series, and it quickly became one of the most insightful design resources in my bookmarks.

The Most Useful UX Resource I've Found This Year

As product designers, we spend a significant amount of time searching for resources that go beyond visual inspiration and actually improve how we think about problems.

Most articles focus on trends, UI patterns, or redesigns. While those can be helpful, they rarely explain how experienced teams identify user pain points and make product decisions.

Recently, I discovered Razorpay's Fix My Itch series:

https://razorpay.com/m/fix-my-itch/

What immediately stood out was its focus on real-world product problems. Instead of showcasing polished interfaces, the content explores friction points, user frustrations, and opportunities for improvement through thoughtful design and product thinking.

Why I Found It Valuable

It focuses on problems before solutions

The strongest design work begins with understanding user pain points. The Fix My Itch series demonstrates how to identify and analyze those problems before jumping into interface changes.

It encourages product thinking

Good designers don't just design screens. They understand business goals, user needs, trade-offs, and system constraints. The examples in this resource consistently reinforce that mindset.

It helps sharpen observation skills

Many of the best product opportunities are hidden in everyday annoyances. This resource trains designers to notice those moments and think critically about how they can be improved.

It is practical and relatable

The examples feel grounded in real experiences rather than hypothetical design exercises, making the lessons easier to apply in everyday product work.

Who Should Read It

• Product Designers

• UX Designers

• Design Students

• Product Managers

• Anyone interested in solving user problems through thoughtful design

Final Thoughts

The best resources don't just teach design methods—they change how you observe the world around you.

Fix My Itch is one of those resources. It has helped me think more deeply about user frustrations, identify opportunities more effectively, and approach design challenges with a stronger problem-solving mindset.

If you're looking for a resource that strengthens product thinking rather than just visual design skills, I highly recommend giving it a read.
